hyps.why: With edge 0->2 removed, node 2 depends only on node 1's path, so a conv on edge 2->3 has weaker input and adds less.
If edge 0->1 is none, node 1 is zero and a conv on edge 1->3 contributes nothing.
A conv on edge 1->2 processes node 1, which is empty when edge 0->1 is none.
Removing the 0->3 shortcut is much more damaging when edge 2->3 is also absent, leaving the output with few or no inputs.
Without the 0->3 edge, cutting 2->3 removes the main remaining path to the output.
Deleting 1->3 hurts more when the direct 0->3 path is already missing, since output connectivity becomes fragile.
If edge 1->3 is already none, node 1 only feeds node 2, so removing 0->1 loses less.
Adding a residual shortcut where there was none brings a large optimization benefit, whereas replacing an existing op gains less or loses capacity.
Filling an empty edge 2->3 with a conv adds a new learnable path to the output, a bigger gain than swapping out an existing op.
When edge 2->3 is absent, a pooling op on 0->3 becomes a dominant output path, and its lack of parameters hurts accuracy more.
